items.english: "Just look. You've made a clean confession, haven't you, but if you want to see a tiger you needn't go all the way to the zoo — give anyone a litre or two and he'll turn into one, eh? — Why, shall we go and see that tiger over there? — That won't do. I can't shake this little one off, you see, and he looked back at the child again. There's a passage like that too," the host went on, still with an eye on the book. And everyone forgot Nekohachi and the rest and bent their hearts toward the tiger, but to Nekohachi that tiger was like himself. "For foolishness, Yui's part is much the same. Rather your single tiger part may be the honour, with the popularity gathering on the tiger alone, you know — thinking so I mean to do all I can with all my might, you know — Yes indeed, we for our part are rather counting on your tiger — Much obliged, and Fukai smiled wryly and yet was not a little comforted in his heart."
notes: Kept the host's summary as flat reported talk with the inner jeers left as dash-led run-on, and kept the identification line plain.

items.english: "That won't do, eh," Nekohachi said, screwing up his face, "to do that situation in a place like that!"
notes: Kept situation as the English loanword he is mouthing; his misuse is left to show.

items.english: "ufu, fu," a stylish little laugh was heard.
notes: Speaker unattributed in the Japanese, so left unattributed.

items.english: "Before gentlemen like you, for the likes of me to use cheeky English may have been a mistake —" He had thought better of it that this English might come to what they call compromise, but, "anyhow, if that actor they call Fukai lets the critic's puffing talk away the decent human thought he had managed to hold in that fix, and goes carelessly getting into the swing again, that will be trouble, eh."
notes: Kept compromise as his second guess at situation without smoothing it; the apology and the warning are in his own patter, not in the group's critical terms.

data.say: Drafted the Tiger continuation with the paraphrase kept flat and Nekohachi's situation and compromise left misused.
